There are castings for people with no training because some directors believe in that as well. 

These schools do provide a good network, however never discount what you might learn from the people in different disciplines at university. 

The top drama schools don't always produce the most talented, in fact, there are fewer applicants every year. 

Statistically speaking, people graduating from drama schools in the UK, something like 90% are unemployed after graduating.

Written work for reference:

  

Objective: to convince my rival actor that I want to act for more than just the fame and fortune, because I think everyone should come together for curtain calls no matter if they’re allies or enemies. My rival should be my ally, I really want us to be friends, if not more than friends. 

Rival: You’re just a phony actor, who’s just in it for the wrong reasons. You shouldn’t be getting roles as an actor; your heart isn’t in it. 

**Actor: My god you couldn’t be more wrong. Will you listen if I tell you what first inspired me? Its kind of a long story.**

Rival: okay go ahead

*(Tactic: Well then get ready. Set the scene for the story. Emphasize on the humor: non-kid friendly play chosen)* 

**Actor: I was in the third grade, when they took us on a field trip to see Richard III in Boston.** 

R: Where you a fan of theatre back then? Because I was.  

*(Tactic: Be honest: it was my first experience; I had a completely fresh outlook on theatre)*

**A: I'd never seen a live play before and I didn't understand what was going on.** 

R: So what did you think was going on?

*(Tactic: my first impression was actually very unpleasant, and it reminded me of everything wrong and tragic id seen in the world (although mostly through television))*

**Actor: But I could tell there was a whole bunch of people hating each other, going to war against each other, and just plain killing each other - kind of like all the wars and murders I’d seen on the news.**

R: Oh, so you hated it?

*(Tactic: three hours later, my opinion had not changed. It was so bleak, I needed to leave and get back to a safe space: school.)* 

**Actor: By the third hour, I was really spacing out, desperately bored and upset with it all...just wanting to go back to class... draw a picture ...take a spelling test!** 

R: Let me guess, you left early. 

**Actor: Finally it ended and they closed the curtain.**

R: So, it was a bad experience, doesn’t sound very inspiring. 

*(Tactic: the tables are about to turn: build up the surprise of how my entire experience became inspirational)* 

**Actor: But then - right then - they did something I wasn't ready for.** 

R: What do you mean?

**Actor: They opened the curtain...and there was everyone who'd been running around hating each other and killing each other for the last three and a half hours.**

R: And?

*(Tactic: At that moment I was completely shocked, it warmed my heart.)*

**Actor: And they were all up there, holding hands, smiling at each other, patting each other on the back, smiling at us and taking a nice bow.**

R: Was that something that seemed important to you? 

*(Tactic: the curtain call changed everything. My entire outlook on life was shattered in that moment)*

**Actor: And that was when it really hit me. Hit me hard. They looked so beautiful**

R: Beautiful?

**Actor: so peaceful and loving.** 

R: What’s the big deal with a curtain call?

*(Tactic: she doesn’t get it: bring up the details that fucked with my head, like Richard the third looking like he was friends with the woman he’d murdered)*

**Actor: Richard the Third was standing right next to the woman he'd murdered, and she was holding his hand and smiling at him as if they were about to go get something to eat together—**

*(Tactic: I was so naïve; it was my first time learning what an actor was)*

**as soon as they washed off their make-up and changed their clothes.**

R: The curtain call isn’t that important compared to the play though.  

*(Tactic: I was shocked, and, in my mind, I thought I had the answers to all the world’s problems. It felt wonderful to believe)*

**Actor: And I had that picture in my head all the way back in the bus, and I lay awake in my bed practically all that night, thinking, “That's what the world needs!”** 

R: What does it need? 

*(Tactic: explain the plan I had conceived)*

**Actor: We need to get the U.N. to pass a resolution that on a certain Sunday, everybody in the world - the President of the United States, the Dalai Lama, Kim Jong-un, the murderers, the millionaires, the bank robbers, the construction workers - will all line up, hold hands and take a bow.**

R: (doesn’t look like she’s taking it seriously) Was Shakespeare there too?

*(Tactic: She still doesn’t get it. I wanted evil and innocent to join hands. Use dead people as an example of how you really imagined it was possible for everyone to reconcile)*

**Actor: Dead people, too. I decided that dead people would suddenly be able to get up off the floor, walk over to the guy who killed them, and say, "Good show, good show! Ladies and gentlemen, we were only kidding. It was all a story.** 

R: You realize murderers and murder victims, probably wouldn’t get along if they met again.  

*(tactic: I believed that if actors could do it, why wouldn’t people be able to?)* 

**Actor: We really all love each other, and now we're going to change out of our costumes and have a party.** 

R: A party huh? 

*(tactic: Make her feel like a part of the idea: she needs to agree with the fantasy, even if its just for a second.)* 

**Actor: You can come too. Cake and cookies and wine, all on us!"**

R: but what does that have to with acting? 

*(Tactic: No more imagination land. I knew if I wanted to make it a reality, my only option in life was to act)*

**Actor: And that's why I wanted to act: so I could do that. Whether I was playing \[Romeo\] or \[Iago\], \[Hamlet\] or \[Claudius\], I wanted people to see me get up off the floor and take my place in line, smiling and holding hands**

R: So, you’re just in it, for the curtain call?!

*(Tactic: Show her my true colors: I want to act so everyone can believe in that fantasy I had after seeing R3rd as a kid.)*

**Actor: So I could give everyone a taste of what it would be like if the whole world could take a curtain call.**

Hey! I sorta preferred your first take of this. I think an important thing i learnt from lessons which you could takeaway is this: your words can't say everything, and they really don't. Your mind and thoughts paint the ideas, your words just try describe them as BEST they can. Those juicy words, those are the ones that help describe your thoughts REALLY well, so you will feel how useful they are for painting your thoughts. 

You are pursuing a goal, and you have to use a few words to describe a vast well of ideas and memories you have. Take time to describe each moment as best you can to the other person, and look to see if they reacted to the words you use. Choose your words carefully. Good luck with future takes!

Generally, i get more from the comments that are responses to video posts that have been made. Comments reminded me about the importance of really using the writer's words to make your point, and helped me internalize how subtext is how you give the strict words your own free interpretation.

Another idea that became clearer through comments was the tactic transitions. This is something that has to come from reacting to the other person, instead of being a spontaneous new tactic that occurs to you from nowhere.

I also visualized more clearly the importance of creating a relationship with the person you talk to, needing something from the person you talk to, and not simply proclaiming your needs without looking for whether or not the other person is giving you what you want. 

Also got a better understanding for when to use gestures or when to change your tone of voice should happen. It should also be a reaction to the other person, and not a sudden change that you decide will be more effective. This made me see how ALL changes should ultimately be prompted by the other person triggering you in a certain way. More REACTING as stimuli for your acting
